outcomes: Execution facts leave the native engine while work runs, followed by the original persisted terminal session
The session reporter uploads what explains a run: every verdict-bearing record and the transcript of each task that does not pass, about half the bytes of the recorded stream
A failed or canceled graph retains its actual verdict while a reporting outage leaves replayable state
A log reporter receives the same live event stream through its own selector and credential, independently of the session reporter
nonGoals: Interpreting CI policy, owning source-hosting credentials, or updating provider checks
Reporting admission, pre-execution failure or executor loss as fabricated task results
Establishing repository/provider provenance, same-principal isolation, or a metadata/network sandbox

requirements.text: Each selected capability (session-reporter, log-reporter) subscribes to the session event stream on its own and receives persisted events while work runs. Reporting finalizes on success, failure and cancellation. The session reporter sends plan.json whole before any other frame, best-effort, and closes session.json before events.jsonl closes; the log reporter gets events.jsonl only. Each records its own subscribers.json entry; its failure, or an omitted plan, changes no other delivery and no verdict.

A cursor per capability retains provider identity, per-artifact sequence and offset, why plan.json was omitted, and at most one exact pending chunk before transmission. An acknowledgement binds the whole chunk identity; a lost one replays the same bytes. sessions replay requires an exact finalized session id, replays only selected capabilities not yet delivered (an unsent plan.json first), rewrites only their entries, uses fresh credentials, and runs no workload DAG or lifecycle hooks.

The authoritative CLI captures and removes every capability's selection and token before extension setup, hooks and repository tasks. Only the capability's own provider process receives its token: never a task, a hook or the other capability's provider. A hosted run passes none; the protocol carries the run credential. Provider stderr and arbitrary error payloads are not echoed. Selection does not establish trust in a repository manifest/runtime, nor prevent same-UID, file, metadata or network access.

Limit chunks to 64 KiB, response lines to 96 KiB, RPCs to 5 s and 3 attempts. Live chunks wait for a full frame or 10 s (session reporter) or 2 s (log reporter). Each drain/replay stops 30 s after the last ACK or 5 min after it starts, naming the limit; cancellation caps it to 2 s, verdict unchanged. Checkpoint reads stop at 192 KiB; replayed session.json and sent plan.json at 16 MiB. Pending records lead sessions.keep; the oldest inactive expire with a diagnostic. Active locks permit temporary excess.

The session reporter sends spec-verification.json last, once the events final marker is acknowledged; the engine writes it before reporting ends. Its frames stop at 8 MiB. When it is absent, too large, unreadable or refused, the reporter quit, or the limits end, the worker omits it, records why, restarts no reporter, and keeps the delivery complete: no diagnostic, verdict or exit code changes. A checkpoint that completed without it stays complete.

The session reporter sends a view of events.jsonl that drops every progress event and the debug lines of a task that ends success or skipped; events.jsonl on disk and the log reporter keep every byte. From a task's first debug line to its task:end, the view holds that task's task:event records as byte ranges and releases them in stream order just before its task:end. A batch line belongs to each member it names, and a shared line leaves at the first member that fails. A session:end record or the final marker releases what is still held; past 1,000,000 held records, the task that holds the most sends live. Each decision depends only on earlier records, so every sequence keeps its bytes after a retry, a reporter restart, and an engine restart or replay, which rebuild the view from offset 0. Checkpoint version 2 records the view cursor beside the raw offset subscribers.json acknowledges; a version 1 checkpoint that sent events keeps raw framing.

A selected capability whose provider the engine cannot prepare warns once, retains the session for replay, and changes no other delivery and no verdict. When the selector names an extension the workspace does not load, or one that serves no such command there, the warning names the selector or the extension. It echoes no other cause: one may carry provider output.
